text:
sasha: Heads up — canary rollout for release/2026-03-17 (PR #4123) is showing a clear p95/p99 spike on streaming endpoints (EventSource). p95 from 60ms -> 220ms, p99 to ~1.1s. Canary traffic pinned down to eu-west-1.

jonah: CI perf job flagged this too: `ci/perf-streaming` failed threshold. Baseline vs head: 18% throughput drop, 3x amplification in tail.

ci-bot: perf/regression: job ci/perf-streaming failed on runner-7. Regression window: 2 commits (abc123 -> def456).

eva: I ran a quick flamegraph on the canary instance. Top time slices are in our protocol serialization path and the new kernel-router. Snippet:
```
  35.4%  runtime_proto::serialize_frame
  22.1%  runtime::kernel_router::choose_kernel
  11.0%  runtime::sse_emitter::flush_buffer
  5.6%   kv_cache::lookup_miss_path
```

mike: Wait, kernel_router spike? We only changed framing in PR #4123, not kernel selection. Which commit did kernel changes?

jonah: commit def456 touched `protocol/sse` framing but also included a small refactor in `runtime/kernel_router` to avoid a lock. It changed a hot-path conditional that used to short-circuit for quantized models. I think the routing logic regresses some quantized path into a slower generic kernel.

sasha: Also noticing more KV-cache misses for streaming tool-calls. Before canary, toolcall policy kept prefix alive across tool handshake; new handshake flow sends an explicit `reset_context` on tool call start. That increases KVC miss rate and forces full serialization more often.

jonah: Reproduced locally with bench-driver: run `bench/stream --seq-len=128 --parallel=50` on HEAD vs v2026-03-16. Trace output:
```
HEAD: avg_latency=0.185s p95=0.212s p99=1.03s
v2026-03-16: avg_latency=0.058s p95=0.062s p99=0.12s

perf trace:
  sse_write -> blocked 42ms waiting for serialize_frame
  serialize_frame -> encode_proto 28ms (due to reserializing full tool inputs)
  kernel_router -> choose_generic_kernel 8ms (was 0.7ms before short-circuit)
```

eva: The serialization cost grows with every extra kv-miss because we rebuild prefixes and re-encode tool metadata. If kernel routing also picks non-quantized kernels, the combined effect amplifies tail due to increased token gen time + bigger frames.

mike: Good catch. Any quick bisect candidate? We should bisect between abc123 and def456.

jonah: I ran `git bisect` already. Culprit was def456 but the measurable regression is the interaction between `protocol/sse` change and `kernel_router` refactor — both in same PR. So revert needs to be surgical.

sasha: Can we hotfix by reverting only the kernel_router conditional change and keep the framing fix? That might restore kernel short-circuiting while preserving protocol behavior.

jonah: Patch idea: reintroduce the quantized-model fast path: in `kernel_router::choose()` if model.quantized && seq_len < 512 -> pick `q8_kern` early. 2-line change.

mike: I'll test that locally. If that brings kernel_router latency down, we still need to address the KV reset on tool-call.

eva: For the KV issue, I propose we change handshake to `soft_reset` flag instead of full `reset_context`, and preserve KV prefixes for active streaming sessions. Minimal change to protocol and backward-compatible.

sasha: While you all test, I'm going to mark the canary rollout as blocked and pause further promotion. deploy-bot, hold rollout.

deploy-bot: Canary promotion paused for release/2026-03-17. Rollout status: BLOCKED. Reason: perf regression detected (eng-runtime).

ci-bot: Addendum: regression test added to ci/perf-streaming to detect increased serialize_frame time >15ms.

jonah: Quick local results with kernel short-circuit revert patch: p95 down to 68ms, p99 140ms. Throughput back within 4% of baseline. KV soft_reset test reduces serialize_frame by ~18% in bench runs.

mike: Patch PR #4130 opened with kernel fix and bench numbers. PR #4131 opened with soft_reset change. Both marked `rollout-blocker`.

sasha: Plan for tomorrow: land PR #4130 first (kernel), run canary for 30m, then PR #4131; if both green, resume rollout. If either fails, revert full PR #4123 in prod.

eva: Also adding a micro-benchmark in our CI that simulates tool-calls under load to catch this class of regressions earlier.

mike: Thanks team. If anyone finds other hotspots in the flamegraphs, ping me. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: automated revert scheduled if no manual action in 4h.

sasha: A reminder — add an entry to the release notes: "fixed streaming p95 regression caused by kernel-routing and handshake semantics" once merged.

jonah: I'll follow up with a short playbook for diagnosing future SSE+toolcall latencies.

mike: Good work narrowing it down quickly.
